meta.comment: Interactive hotspots. (u,v) are NORMALISED poster coordinates: 0..1 from the TOP-LEFT corner of poster.jpg. They drive both the AR anchors (mapped onto the tracked image plane) and the on-screen Demo Mode. The values below target the v6 poster layout (3 columns under the header/hero). Tweak (u,v) to line each dot up with your printed poster. Optional 'labelDir' (down|up|left|right, default down) sets which side the text label sits so neighbouring labels do not overlap.

hotspots.label: Test case
hotspots.body: A closed rectangular water tank (about 7.5 cm tall) at 293 K with a small warm jet entering at mid-height. The warm jet is lighter than the surrounding water, so buoyancy lifts it and a vertical thermal layer builds up under the ceiling.

hotspots.label: Setup & mesh
hotspots.body: A structured mesh of 1 mm cubic cells (~85,625) fills the tank. Regular cells keep the scheme stable and let the cell-to-cell (C2C) shift maps of rCFD be defined cleanly on every face. With Re ≈ 100 the jet is laminar, so a laminar solver fits — run in Fluent 2022 R2 on Windows 11.

subs.label: Is the flow laminar or turbulent?

hotspots.label: rCFD workflow
hotspots.body: Recurrence CFD runs the expensive flow solve once and records the recurring cell-to-cell (C2C) shift patterns. The cheap replay loop then repeats 600× to transport temperature — with no Navier–Stokes solve during replay. That is the source of the ~263× speed-up.

hotspots.label: Mixing — f_sd
hotspots.body: A pure C2C shift moves heat but does not mix it, leaving sharp interfaces. The face-swap operator restores the missing mixing across every internal face; its single parameter f_sd sets how strongly. It is mass- and energy-conservative, with a 1/8 stability cap that splits strong mixing into inner sweeps.

subs.label: Why is the best f_sd metric-dependent?

hotspots.label: Adiabatic results
hotspots.body: rCFD reproduces the CFD temperature field across the full 600 s at a small fraction of the cost. The rising warm plume, the recirculation vortices and the stratified layer are all captured. The best mixing strength is metric-dependent: f_sd = 0.500 gives the lowest centre-of-gravity error.

subs.label: Why is the best f_sd metric-dependent?

hotspots.label: Wall heat loss
hotspots.body: Letting the top surface lose heat, q = h(T − T∞) with h ≈ 8 W/m²K, stress-tests the reuse idea. Replaying the reused adiabatic database cools the tank by only 0.36 K, against 1.45 K in the full CFD — about 24%. The frozen replay misses the buoyancy-driven overturning that keeps fresh warm fluid at the cooled surface.
